story.iWant: the project scaffolded with required dependencies
story.soThat: I can start building the core service layer
story.tasks: - Ensure required runtime/dev dependencies are declared in package.json and install cleanly with bun install. - Align the source tree with the foundation structure in docs/architecture.md (src/lib/keycloak, src/mcp, src/cli, and subfolders). - Prepare and align .env.example with the configuration contract (Keycloak URL/realm/client, admin credentials, log level). - Review or prepare package.json scripts so later stories can wire cli, mcp, and dev entrypoints.

story-context.acceptanceCriteria: 1) Dependencies installed successfully: from a fresh clone, bun install completes without errors. 2) Required runtime/dev dependencies present: @keycloak/keycloak-admin-client, @modelcontextprotocol/sdk, citty, zod, pino, dotenv are available after install. 3) Project structure matches architecture: src/lib/keycloak, src/lib/keycloak/services, src/mcp (with tools), and src/cli (with commands and utils) exist. 4) Environment template prepared: .env.example exists at repo root and includes KEYCLOAK_URL, KEYCLOAK_REALM, KEYCLOAK_CLIENT_ID, KEYCLOAK_USERNAME, KEYCLOAK_PASSWORD, LOG_LEVEL. 5) Tooling alignment: package.json (or future scripts) is ready to expose cli, mcp, and dev commands consistent with the architecture and tech-spec.

docs.doc: keycloak-commander is defined as an AI-native admin tool whose core is a TypeScript service layer around the Keycloak Admin API; this story ensures the dependencies and structure exist so that service layer can be implemented cleanly.

Architecture specifies a service-first layout (src/lib/keycloak, src/mcp, src/cli) and Bun-based setup commands; this story creates that skeleton and aligns .env.example with the documented configuration contract.

Epic 1 and Story 1.1 formalize FR1–FR4 as a foundation: project structure, dependencies, configuration, and connectivity; this story is explicitly scoped to scaffolding without domain-specific behavior.

The Epic 1 tech spec defines config.ts, client.ts, errors.ts, and logger.ts as foundational modules with Zod-based configuration, a singleton Keycloak client wrapper, standardized error types, and Pino logging; this story prepares the directories and dependency set those modules rely on.

code.note: No new implementation code is expected for this story beyond project scaffolding; it creates directories and dependency declarations so later Epic 1 stories can introduce config, client, error, and logging modules.

dependency.existingPackagesSummary: SvelteKit, Vitest, Playwright, Storybook, Tailwind, Drizzle ORM, and TypeScript are already present and provide the web, testing, and data scaffolding this story must keep compatible with.

story-context.constraints: - Follow the service-first architecture from docs/architecture.md; this story must not bake domain-specific logic into the scaffold. - Keep credentials and secrets out of the repo; .env.example must use obvious placeholders and align with the security constraints in PRD and architecture. - Maintain compatibility with the existing SvelteKit, testing, and database tooling already defined in package.json and architecture.md.

tests.standards: For this foundation story, validation focuses on reproducible installs and structural correctness rather than unit tests; later Epic 1 stories add Zod-validated config and connection tests aligned with the Epic 1 tech-spec and architecture test strategy.
tests.locations: Existing unit tests live under src/**/*.spec.ts and e2e tests under e2e/**/*.test.ts; no new automated tests are mandatory for this story, but future config and client modules will add coverage in those locations.
tests.ideas: - Run bun install on a fresh clone and verify it succeeds and installs the new IAM-related dependencies. - Assert that src/lib/keycloak, src/lib/keycloak/services, src/mcp (with tools), and src/cli (with commands and utils) all exist after scaffolding. - Verify .env.example contains the documented Keycloak and logging variables and no real secrets. - Confirm package.json either already exposes or is ready to expose cli, mcp, and dev scripts consistent with the architecture.
